caption: Table 2. Evaluation targets and the evidence needed to interpret them.
rows: Candidate discrimination
Labelled candidate records admitted by a gate
Does not establish coverage outside that gate.
Occurrence recovery
Annotated secret locations in eligible sources
Requires a stated source boundary and matching relation.
Credential discovery
Distinct credential values or defined equivalence groups
One recovered copy does not imply all locations were found.
Asset pairing
Credential–asset relationships in the labelled pairing set
Does not establish all generic credentials have identifiable assets.
Warning response
Warnings, affected values, or confirmed actions under a declared workflow
Detection, bypass, revocation and cleanup require separate outcomes.

caption: Table 3. Study-level evidence map. Statements concern the assessed source versions, not independently rerun tools. Detailed anchors and appraisal are in Online Resource 1.
rows: GitHub measurement [1]
Format-constrained searches and snapshot scans. Unit: Candidate key occurrence and unique key.
Contextual manual appraisal on sampled candidates; uncertainty retained. Not a census of every credential format.
Credential Digger [2]
Regex scanner followed by path/snippet/similarity filters. Unit: Discovery emitted by the first scanner.
Manual samples from retained and rejected discoveries. Filter-stage false negatives do not cover secrets missed by regex.
PassFinder [3]
Candidate-file search followed by string/context models. Unit: Password or qualifying API-key occurrence in selected files.
Manually annotated 5,000-file end-to-end set. End-to-end within candidate files differs from repository-wide ascertainment.
Industrial warning workflow [4]
Warnings emitted by an internal commit-time scanner. Unit: Warning outcome and developer response.
Usage events and respondent accounts; potential secrets not all independently confirmed. Bypass is not equivalent to confirmed live exposure.
SecretBench [5]
Regex-informed repository selection; TruffleHog/Gitleaks candidate union. Unit: Labelled candidate occurrence; unique values also described.
Independent contextual annotation and discussion; no live use of credentials. Candidate-relative ground truth; repeated values and occurrences differ.
Nine-tool comparison [6]
Runs on SecretBench repositories with date filtering. Unit: Exact-location recovery or repository-level value recovery.
Similarity matching and sampled manual checking. Matching relation and unit alter the score; temporal snapshot alignment matters.
AssetHarvester [7]
Python/database subset of SecretBench; remove unmatched assets. Unit: Secret–asset pair.
Two-person contextual asset identification; disagreement resolution. Pair-level recovery among identifiable assets is not generic secret recall.
KeySentinel [8]
Cross-platform file collection and tool-assisted candidate labelling. Unit: Labelled secret occurrence across GitHub/PyPI/WeChat.
Candidate aggregation plus manual annotation. Broad platforms do not establish coverage of all tool-invisible positives.
Android tool review and experiment [9]
App collection; processing eligibility and adapted tool outputs. Unit: Detected string/key with category restrictions.
Manual checking; recall replaced by overlap because complete labels unavailable. Union overlap is not absolute recall; unsupported types differ across tools.
SecretBench duplication audit [10]
SecretBench language subset; exact/near/unique conditions. Unit: Candidate code context.
Original labels; controlled split scenarios. Duplication relation and test novelty must be declared.
Learning to detect hardcoded secrets [11]
Language-restricted SecretBench; exact contextual deduplication. Unit: Candidate/context classification.
Inherited benchmark labels; main versus unseen C# split. Language holdout tests a specific transfer axis, not all deployments.
Issue-report detection [12]
Keyword-retrieved issues; regex candidates and benign filtering. Unit: Issue-body/candidate pair.
Manual context labels and additional rater subset; no live validation. Classifier performance is conditional on upstream retrieval/extraction.
Secretron [13]
SecretBench repository split; cross-language and obfuscation tests. Unit: Candidate/context label; separate Android warning yield.
Inherited labels and manual app-output review. Repository split is useful but not automatically credential-family disjointness.
LaTeXpOsEd [14]
Preprint source/comment pipeline and synthetic benchmark. Unit: Sensitive-entity category/span; broader than credentials.
Controlled synthetic snippets plus targeted real-output manual review. Synthetic label completeness does not establish natural-population coverage.
SenScanner [15]
Code files combined with generated natural-language statements. Unit: Secret-level occurrence, component label, or file label.
Controlled mixed-text labels; distinct component and pipeline metrics. Constructed mixtures differ from naturally occurring issue/code distributions.

caption: Table 4. Proposed reporting contract. These are inspectable reporting requirements, not a validated certification score.
rows: Population
Source kind, acquisition dates, eligibility, processing failures
Identifies what source-level conclusions represent.
Candidate gate
Rules/models, versions, order, exclusions and emitted identifiers
Separates discovery from downstream classification.
Unit
Occurrence, value, project, pair, warning or action; grouping relation
Makes numerator and denominator interpretable.
Labels
Positive meaning, annotators/adjudication, unknown handling, time and authority
Separates contextual labels from current operational validity.
Matching
Normalization, location requirements, similarity rule and threshold
Defines which output recovers which labelled target.
Partition
Grouping keys, deduplication stage, tuning boundary, transfer axis
Makes the intended novelty of the test population explicit.
Metric and uncertainty
Raw counts; averaging; sample design and resampling unit
Prevents incompatible weighted or sampled scores from being conflated.
Workflow
Verification mode, triage and observed intervention outcome
Avoids equating detector output with remediation.
